description: Craft the ultimate Tonkotsu Ramen experience right in your kitchen with this authentic pork bone broth recipe. This rich, milky white broth is the soul of any great ramen bowl, slow-simmered to extract maximum flavor and collagen. Prepare to impress with a deeply savory and incredibly creamy foundation for your homemade ramen.

instructions.title: Prepare and Soak the Bones
instructions.text: Thoroughly clean all pork bones under cold running water to remove any blood or impurities. Place the cleaned bones in a large stockpot and cover them completely with cold water. Soak for 2-4 hours, changing the water several times, until the water remains mostly clear. This step is crucial for a clean-tasting broth.

instructions.title: Blanch the Bones
instructions.text: Drain the soaking water. Return the bones to the stockpot, cover again with fresh cold water, and bring to a rolling boil over high heat. Boil vigorously for 10-15 minutes, continuously skimming off all the dark scum that rises to the surface. Drain the bones and rinse each piece thoroughly under cold water to remove any remaining scum. Wash the stockpot clean.

instructions.title: Begin the Long Simmer
instructions.text: Place the cleaned and blanched bones back into the clean stockpot. Add 6-8 liters of fresh cold water, ensuring the bones are fully submerged. Bring the water to a rapid, rolling boil over high heat. Once boiling, reduce the heat slightly to maintain a vigorous, rolling simmer. Continue to skim any rising scum for the first hour of simmering.

instructions.title: Add Aromatics and Continue Simmering
instructions.text: After the initial skimming, add the sliced ginger, halved garlic head, and white parts of the green onions to the pot. If using, add the kombu and dried shiitake mushrooms. Maintain a strong, rolling simmer, uncovered, for 12-18 hours. Top up with boiling water every 2-3 hours to keep the bones fully submerged and ensure maximum extraction. The broth should gradually turn milky white and opaque.

instructions.title: Strain the Broth
instructions.text: Carefully remove all bones and aromatics from the pot using tongs or a slotted spoon. Strain the broth through a fine-mesh sieve into another large heatproof container. For an even clearer broth, line the sieve with cheesecloth. Gently press any solids to extract remaining liquid, but do not crush the bones as this can release undesirable flavors.

instructions.title: Emulsify and Reduce (Optional)
instructions.text: Return the strained broth to a clean pot. Bring it back to a strong boil and whisk vigorously for 10-15 minutes. This action helps to emulsify the fat and collagen, creating the characteristic creamy texture and opaque white color of authentic Tonkotsu broth. Reduce the broth to your desired concentration and richness.

instructions.title: Cool and Store
instructions.text: Allow the finished Tonkotsu broth to cool completely before storing. You can skim off any solidified fat from the top once cooled, if desired. Transfer the broth to airtight containers. It can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days or frozen for several months, ready to be used as a base for your homemade ramen.

tips: Soaking and blanching the bones are crucial steps to remove impurities and ensure a clean, clear, and pure-tasting broth. Do not skip them for the best results.
Maintaining a vigorous, rolling boil throughout the simmering process is key to emulsifying the fat and collagen, which creates the signature milky white color and rich texture of Tonkotsu broth.
Do not season the broth with salt until you are ready to serve your ramen. This allows for maximum versatility and prevents over-salting when combined with tare (ramen seasoning).
